analysis.title: Revisiting Galp, oil up despite Iran diplomacy + Energy Daily 27/10/26
key_insights: Oil remains near its 6-month high despite October Middle East exports in double digits and renewed regional diplomacy with Iran. The spec sales comment says markets have belatedly priced higher-for-longer scenarios and near-term escalation risk, and that potential fresh export disruption outweighs higher actual volumes.

Hezbollah is reportedly preparing new attacks on Israel after receiving funds from Iran, and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Red Sea vessels have picked up. Trump is reportedly still considering restarting military action after next week's midterms.
Diplomatic channels are open between Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey, Qatar, Oman and Iran, but the desk says a diplomatic outcome is unlikely to look probable until the US decides on a path forward.

Galp 3Q26 beat by 4% at operating level, 7% on net income and 14% on CFFO, and raised FY EBITDA guidance. The shares fell 11% on the collapse of the Moeve downstream merger talks and the Brazil election result.

The Moeve collapse is the second recent case of Galp management being too optimistic on a major commercial issue. It also lowers the perceived probability of M&A focused on a streamlined Upstream entity. Management says it remains committed to carving out Downstream and no partnership talks are currently active.

UBS (Josh Stone) retains Buy on Galp. Remaining catalysts are Namibia drilling news, a possible step-up in buybacks next year and a supportive macro backdrop. Brazil uncertainty and European windfall tax risk mean investors are likely to feel no urgency to re-engage.
Lula's re-election in Brazil continues the export levy that has weighed on Galp's relative performance this year, but the desk sees no incremental negatives from it.

EQT will buy Range Resources in a $13 billion all-stock deal to create the largest US natural gas producer, betting on LNG export and power generation demand. UBS is positive long term, but the deal is near-term dilutive to per-share estimates.
Ovintiv will buy Logan Energy for about $890 million including debt, in an all-cash deal that adds to its Montney position. UBS calls it a positive step in Ovintiv's Montney consolidation.
IEA head Birol does not expect energy markets in 2027 to return to pre-war levels. The Iran war began in late February.

Equity desk: S&P +0.7% and Nasdaq +0.8% on Monday. Semis rose about 2.7% and AI winners 2% on AI IPO filings, while neoclouds fell on AI infrastructure debt concerns. Meta plans to raise up to $95bn for AI buildout, starting with $35bn of common and preferred shares.

Asia is higher on the US tech read-across: KOSPI +4.6%, SK Hynix +5.5% on reports of a further 50-60tr won capital return, Samsung +4.2%, Nikkei above 2% to about 63,500, Advantest +10%, SoftBank +7%, HSI -0.2%.

Brent briefly traded above $117 on renewed US-Iran escalation risk after the midterms, then eased below $115 as diplomacy resurfaced. The desk calls oil the biggest threat to the early recovery rally.
The Fed is expected to hold on Wednesday. The desk sees hyperscaler capex versus monetisation from MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN later in the week as the real test for the rebound.

European flows Monday were 55/45 better for sale on turnover about 15% above the YTD run rate. Banks were better bid on French and UK names after summer supply, while pharma, semis, software and energy saw supply.
HSBC earnings commentary on deposit competition hurt the European banks narrative: SX7E futures -65bps and HSBC -5% in Hong Kong.

market_movers.rationale: Galp (Portugal) beat 3Q26 estimates and raised FY EBITDA guidance, but the Moeve merger collapse and Brazil result hit the shares by 11%. UBS keeps Buy and sees an opportunity like the post-Namibia correction.
UBS is positive on the all-stock RRC acquisition despite near-term per-share dilution, citing long-term value opportunities.
UBS updates estimates after the Logan Energy bolt-on, which strengthens its Montney position.
Bharat Petroleum's Q2 EBITDA beat on strong refining margins. Rising capex and net debt in volatile crude support UBS's Neutral rating.
United Tractors' Q3 NPAT rose 45% QoQ excluding one-offs booked in Q226, and delayed mining approvals may support Q4 momentum.

sector_views.rationale: Oil is near a 6-month high, and the IEA expects energy markets not to return to pre-war levels in 2027. UBS research is positive on EQT and Ovintiv M&A and on India offshore E&P.
HSBC's commentary on deposit competition hurt the sector narrative, and SX7E futures were down 65bps.

earnings_insights: Galp 3Q26 (reported): beat by 4% at operating level, 7% on net income and 14% on CFFO versus expectations, with FY EBITDA guidance raised. Shares fell 11%.
Bharat Petroleum Q2 (reported): EBITDA beat estimates on strong refining margins.
United Tractors Q3 (reported): NPAT up 45% QoQ excluding one-offs booked in Q226.
China Oilfield Services 9M26 (reported): net profit up 1% YoY, with a loss still a major drag.
HSBC earnings (reported) included commentary on deposit competition that was unhelpful for European banks.
Hyperscaler earnings from MSFT, GOOGL and AMZN are due later this week.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Oil is near a 6-month high on renewed US-Iran escalation risk after the midterms, easing as diplomacy resurfaced.
The desk treats the Fed as a non-event and focuses on hyperscaler capex versus monetisation.

risk_factors: Renewed US-Iran military action after the midterms could disrupt Middle East oil exports.
Escalation by Hezbollah, the Houthis or Israel could spread the conflict.
AI infrastructure debt concerns weighed on neoclouds, and hyperscaler capex may fail to show monetisation.
Brazil policy uncertainty and a possible European windfall tax weigh on Galp.
Management credibility on Galp after two overly optimistic calls.
Deposit competition could pressure European bank earnings.
vol_and_positioning: Equity flows Monday were 55/45 better for sale, with turnover about 15% above the YTD run rate.
Healthcare was 26% of turnover and better for sale. Banks were 15% and better bid on demand for French and UK names. Industrials were 11% and Technology 10%, both with supply.
Growth and Momentum factors recovered, and market-cap outperformed equal weight.
geopolitical: US-Iran war that began in late February, with Trump reportedly considering restarting military action after next week's midterms.
Regional diplomacy with Iran involving Saudi Arabia, Pakistan, Turkey, Qatar and Oman, not led by the US.
Hezbollah reportedly preparing new attacks on Israel after receiving funds from Iran, ahead of Israel's election.
Houthis attacked Saudi East-West crude pumping stations and Riyadh airport, and attacks on Red Sea vessels have picked up.
Lula's re-election in Brazil and the continued export levy.
Russian refiners are raising diesel output after export quotas following the Kremlin's supply agreement with the US.

tension_points.bull_case: Oil stays near its 6-month high because markets price higher-for-longer scenarios and near-term escalation risk, with fresh disruption to exports outweighing higher actual volumes.
tension_points.bear_case: October Middle East oil exports are in double digits and regional states are pursuing diplomacy with Iran, which could ease prices.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A US decision on the path forward toward diplomacy rather than a restart of military action after the midterms.
